entry.title: Caffeinated Commits- Day 3
entry.summary:
This is proving to be more difficult...
With a full-time job and living alone, finding the motivation to code beyond what my job demands is really exhausting. On top of that, being unfamiliar not only with the endless Java Collections and their functions but also with Java itself makes LeetCode quite frustrating. I didn’t make much progress today. I skimmed through the Java Collections and the functions they offer, and I managed to solve one question — Longest Common Prefix. No progress on the project today 😔. I’ve also decided that I’ll be posting small snippets like these every day, along with a more detailed weekly post on Sundays, where I’ll go into my approaches and thought process. Thanks for reading!

entry.title: How I Use GitHub Copilot to Review Code and Pull Requests
entry.summary: GitHub Copilot - code review assistant Pull Requests (PR) are a central part of many teams’ workflows. PRs allow us to consolidate changes into a single, manageable unit that can be communicated, discussed, and refined. But this process can be time-consuming. Because of this, I’ve been exploring GitHub copilot code review as a complement to the traditional code review process to reduce this overhead. GitHub Copilot offloads basic reviews to a copilot agent that catches issues like logic bugs, potential performance problems, anti-patterns, and even suggests fixes to improve code quality. When I first started using copilot, I primarily used it in my code editor for autocomplete and code suggestions.
